mechanism_narrative: When WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain deeply depressed while RESIDENTIAL stays elevated, weekday trip generation stays weak and discretionary shopping demand does not recover. This should keep RETAIL_REC below its prior 4-week mean over the next month.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days exceeds the last 28-day mean while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT do not rise from their current depressed levels.

mechanism_narrative: A rebound in GROCERY_PHARM above the zero baseline indicates renewed out-of-home errand frequency and nearby bundle shopping, which spills into retail trips within one to two weeks. If that errand activity persists, RETAIL_REC should move up next.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM crosses from negative to positive and stays above 0 for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within 14 days after GROCERY_PHARM turns positive for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If PARKS and RESIDENTIAL both rise while TRANSIT remains weak, leisure time is being reallocated toward home-based and outdoor local activity rather than shopping trips. That mix should suppress retail-and-recreation mobility over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite simultaneous increases in PARKS and RESIDENTIAL with TRANSIT still below baseline.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-week drop in TRANSIT signals a mobility shock or restriction response that immediately cuts access to retail districts. The retail effect should appear within one week and remain negative unless transit recovers quickly.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls by more than 8 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT is already at -71.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to fall in the next 7 days after a weekly TRANSIT drop greater than 8 points.

mechanism_narrative: When PARKS activity remains very low for several weeks and does not rebound, outdoor leisure substitution is absent and shoppers keep spending time away from retail destinations. That should leave RETAIL_REC below its recent average over the next month.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stays below -25 for 3 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is not lower than the last 28 days after PARKS remains below -25 for three weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES indicates people are resuming clustered errand-and-work routines, which increases incidental retail visits with a short lag. That combination should lift retail-and-recreation mobility within two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase within 14 days even though both GROCERY_PHARM and WORKPLACES trend upward together.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL exceeds +15 while WORKPLACES stays below -25, the metro is in a stay-at-home allocation that reduces nonessential trips and shopping frequency. Under that regime, retail mobility should continue to decline relative to the prior four weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL > 15 and WORKPLACES < -25 for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days while RESIDENTIAL stays above 15 and WORKPLACES stays below -25 for two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A recovery in TRANSIT paired with WORKPLACES indicates restored commuting access and more daytime foot traffic near shopping corridors. Once both improve, retail-and-recreation mobility should move higher after a one-week lag.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES each rise at least 5 points from their prior week values
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve in the following week after both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES rise by at least 5 points.
